payout_quote: A bug bounty is a monetary reward given to ethical hackers for responsibly discovering and reporting a vulnerability or bug to the application's developer.
steps: Create a free HackerOne hacker account.
Browse the public program directory for programs open to all hackers.
Read each program's scope (in-scope domains/assets) and rules of engagement carefully.
Test only in-scope assets ethically and document findings with proof-of-concept.
Submit the report; if valid and unique, the organization pays the bounty per its published severity-based reward structure.
catches: Only valid, unique, in-scope findings are paid — duplicates and out-of-scope reports earn nothing.
Bounty amounts are set per program by severity; no platform-wide payout range.
Testing out of scope can get you banned and may have legal consequences.
Requires real security skills; beginners will spend a lot of time for zero payout.
Private programs are invite-only; new hackers start with public programs only.
biggest_catch: You only get paid for valid, unique, in-scope vulnerabilities — most time spent hunting produces nothing, and out-of-scope testing can get you banned.
eligibility: Free hacker account; ethical security testing skills.
timing: Programs run continuously; bounties paid after report validation and remediation review per program terms.

c1.evidence: HackerOne's own page states the mechanism: 'A bug bounty is a monetary reward given to ethical hackers for responsibly discovering and reporting a vulnerability' and 'Bug bounty programs allow companies to leverage the hacker community.'

c2.evidence: Official terms tie bounties to valid reported vulnerabilities per program — amounts are program-set; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: sign up, find public programs, read scope/rules, test in scope, submit reports.

c4.evidence: Joining and hacking public programs are free; no upfront fee documented.

s1.note: Eligibility is a free account with security skills.

s2.note: Framed as variable per-program bounties; no fixed amount promised.

s3.note: Catches cover duplicate/out-of-scope non-payment, skill requirements, and scope discipline.
